title: Understanding Bluff and Fold in Texas Hold'em
summaryJa: テキサスホールデムの基本的な戦略用語である「ブラフ」と「フォールド」について説明します。ブラフは弱いカードで相手を騙す戦術で、フォールドは手を降りることです。
segments: Texas Hold'em poker has many important words. Two of the most common words are "bluff" and "fold.
" These words help players understand the game better. Let me explain what they mean and how players use them at the table.
A "bluff" is when a player pretends to have a better hand than they really have. For example, a player has only weak cards.
But they bet a lot of money anyway. They want other players to think they have strong cards.
If other players believe the bluff, they will fold their hands. Then the bluff player wins the pot without showing their cards.
A "fold" means a player gives up their hand and stops playing that round. When a player folds, they lose any money they already put in the pot.
But they do not lose any more money. For example, a player bets ten dollars.
Another player bets fifty dollars. The first player does not want to risk fifty dollars.
So they fold. Now the second player can win the pot, or the game continues with other players.
These two words work together in many poker games. One player may bluff with weak cards.
Another player may see the bluff and fold. Or another player may not believe the bluff and call.
Learning when to bluff and when to fold is an important skill. It helps players win more games and have more fun playing Texas Hold'em.
